items.note: It answers the question head-on: Pro at $69 churned 10 of 12 (83%), against 1 of 8 (12.5%) at $49, and it calls the $69 price the main driver. The counts check out. It never ties this to the July increase, though. It guesses at a price change 'around August' and opens with overall churn instead of the Pro question.
It removes the 15 trial accounts and explains why.
Churn is counted as any account with a cancel_month.
It reads like an analyst report, not a CEO brief. It is full of account IDs, several tables, cohort detail and data-cleaning notes.
The limit was at most 5 bullets. The answer has several sections, tables and a 5-item recommendation list on top of that.

The caveats say the sample is small (40 accounts), the percentages are noisy, and the result is a strong correlation, not a proven cause. That covers confidence, though without a clear confidence level.
